# Code Review — 2026-07-16

Scope: full local repo at HEAD `40d8756` — Go pipeline (`internal/press`, `internal/mcp`, `internal/config`, `cmd/symprint`), macOS Swift client, CI workflows, docs/examples.

- [ ] **[Security] Constrain MCP `render_pdf` output paths and stop silent overwrites**
  - **Status quo:** The MCP tool accepts any `output_path` and writes there unconditionally (`internal/mcp/server.go:135`, `internal/press/typst.go:70`); `MkdirAll` even creates arbitrary directory trees. A prompt-injected or misbehaving agent can clobber any user-writable file with PDF bytes — no overwrite check, no containment.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add an optional `[mcp] output_root` config key; when set, reject paths that resolve (after `filepath.Abs`/symlink cleaning) outside it. Independently, refuse to overwrite an existing file unless it starts with `%PDF` or an explicit `overwrite: true` argument is passed. Return a structured error with a hint.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Security] CI never verifies the `meeting` profile's PDF/A-2a + PDF/UA-1 guarantee**
  - **Status quo:** `meeting` promises `a-2a` + `ua-1` (`internal/press/profile.go:117`) and is marketed as "accessible and archivable" (#57), but the render-smoke job only renders report/behoerde/brief and only runs veraPDF against `behoerde.pdf` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:78-95`). The compliance claim is unverified; a template regression would ship silently — the opposite of the README's "fails closed" promise.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add `examples/meeting.md` (and `rechnung.md`) to the render step and run the two veraPDF checks against `meeting.pdf` as well; loop over a profile list instead of hard-coding filenames.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Security] Pin the remaining unpinned CI toolchain (govulncheck, staticcheck)**
  - **Status quo:** All actions are SHA-pinned, but `go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:41`) and `staticcheck version: "latest"` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:36`) pull moving targets — a supply-chain gap and a source of non-reproducible CI failures.
  - **Proposed solution:** Pin `govulncheck@v1.x.y` and a fixed staticcheck version; let Dependabot (already active in the repo) or a periodic chore bump them deliberately.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[UX/DX] `meeting` profile missing from user-facing profile lists (docs drift)**
  - **Status quo:** The registry has five profiles, but the MCP instructions (`internal/mcp/server.go:42`), root `--help` text (`cmd/symprint/main.go:43-53`), `config init` template (`internal/config/config.go:109`), package doc comment (`cmd/symprint/main.go:2`), and README status/table (`README.md:62`, `README.md:141-147`) all still say "brief, behoerde, report, rechnung". AI agents reading the MCP instructions won't discover `meeting` without calling `list_profiles`.
  - **Proposed solution:** Update all five prose sites to include `meeting` (with its PDF/A+UA guarantee); pair with the Architecture item below so the lists can't drift again.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[UX/DX] Broken config.toml is silently ignored by every command**
  - **Status quo:** All four config-consuming commands swallow `config.Load()` errors and fall back to defaults (`cmd/symprint/render.go:41-44`, `cmd/symprint/doctor.go:18-20`, `cmd/symprint/validate.go:21-23`, `cmd/symprint/mcp.go:18-20`). A TOML typo silently reverts profile/timeout/font settings — contradicting the project's "typos fail loudly" contract for frontmatter.
  - **Proposed solution:** Extract one `loadConfigOrWarn()` helper that prints `warning: config ignored (<path>): <err>` to stderr (and a `warnings` field in `--json` mode), then falls back. Erroring out is optional; warning is the minimum.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[Architecture] Generate profile prose from the registry (single source of truth)**
  - **Status quo:** The profile list is duplicated as hand-written prose in at least four places (root help, MCP instructions, config template, README) and has already drifted once (see UX/DX item). `press.All()` (`internal/press/profile.go:131`) already exposes everything needed.
  - **Proposed solution:** Build the profile lines for `cmd/symprint/main.go` Long text, `internal/mcp/server.go` SetInstructions, and `internal/config/config.go` DefaultConfigTOML at runtime from `press.All()` (name, title, key guarantee). Add a README check or make target for the remaining manual site.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Architecture] Config loader cache forces declaration-order-dependent tests**
  - **Status quo:** `internal/config` caches its loader process-wide with no reset, so `doctor_test.go:13-20` must literally be the first declared test in the package and carries a warning comment forbidding reordering — a fragile invariant that will break silently when someone adds a test.
  - **Proposed solution:** Export a `ResetForTest()` (or accept a loader/config via dependency injection into the cobra commands, as `engineFromConfig` already hints). Remove the ordering constraint and its comment.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[Performance] Cache engine probe and materialized assets across renders in the MCP server**
  - **Status quo:** Every render spawns `typst --version` (`internal/press/render.go:108` → `internal/press/engine.go:58`) and re-materializes all templates plus both Inter TTFs into a fresh temp dir (`internal/press/typst.go:40-54`). Fine for one-shot CLI, but the long-lived MCP server pays two extra process/IO round-trips per document.
  - **Proposed solution:** Memoize `DetectTypst` per (binOverride, process) with a short TTL, and materialize templates/fonts once into a per-process cache dir (contents are immutable embedded assets), keeping only `meta.json`/`body.md`/`main.typ` per-render.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / medium impact

## Conclusion

The codebase is small, well-tested, and consistent. The highest-leverage first move is the **CI veraPDF gap for the `meeting` profile** — it's a few YAML lines and directly protects the product's core compliance promise. Fix the profile-list drift in the same sitting (same theme: five profiles, four documented).
